text:
dana: quick thought — when a client cancels midstream over HTTP/3 we need to decide how the gateway signals upstream: hard RST vs a soft stop. with multiplexing we can’t just tear down the connection w/o affecting siblings.
ryan: +1. prefer per-stream soft signal first. RST loses telemetry and wastes work. soft stop tells model to stop producing new chunks but finish current token window.
leah: can we define a minimal handshake header for that? something like `x-proxy-cancel: soft` and an ack from upstream `x-upstream-cancel-ack: ok` so the gateway knows it can release backpressure resources.
matt: sketching a tiny state machine — client-stream -> proxy-forward -> (soft-cancel) -> upstream drains current frame -> ack -> proxy close stream. if upstream ignores soft, gateway escalates to RST after timeout.
sheryl: important: billing + logging. if we do soft-cancel we need deterministic checkpoints to bill partial tokens and attribute traces. otherwise customers will freak.
dana: yea — plan: 1) soft-cancel header, 2) small grace window (configurable by route), 3) final cutoff where gateway RSTs. grace window affects latency SLOs.
ryan: edge case: preemptive admission — higher-priority tenant can preempt a low-priority stream. do we reuse same soft-cancel flow? seems fine but need to track reason codes: `preempt` vs `client_cancel` vs `network` so upstream can decide side effects.
leah: propose reason mapping: `rc=client_cancel|preempt|net_err`. reason code in `x-proxy-cancel-reason`. also record last-seen kv-cache offset for resumability and billing.
matt: small config example for route:

```
route:
  path: /v1/generate
  cancel_policy:
    mode: soft_then_hard
    soft_timeout_ms: 250
    hard_timeout_ms: 2000
    reason_codes: [client_cancel, preempt, network]
```

ryan: will this play nice with QUIC flow control? soft-cancel should only affect logical stream; we must not close connection-level flow windows. on severe memory pressure we may need global admission to pause new streams.
sheryl: about checkpoints: we should inject a checkpoint header every N tokens like `x-checkpoint-offset: 1024` so billing and resume can tie to that boundary. not every model supports offsets, so gateway must fallback to token-estimates.
dana: ops note — instrument metrics: cancel_reason, soft_ack_latency, escalations_count. we can use those to tune defaults.
infra-bot: deploy note: rollout in three phases: (1) propagate header contract to dedicated-only (canary), (2) enable soft cancel on default in staging, (3) wide release. watch: `cancel-escalation` alert.
leah: one more: how do we handle side-effectful responses (webhooks, DB writes) where duplicate or partial outputs are unsafe? soft-cancel can't leave upstream in unknown state. maybe require route-level side_effect_policy = always-idempotent | require-confirm | disallow-soft-cancel.
matt: agree. require-confirm would mean upstream must reply with finalization ack before gateway forwards final status back to client. adds latency but safer.
dana: next steps: I'll write a short RFC with state machine ASCII, header names, and default timers. can we get quick reviews? pinging @ryan @leah @sheryl for design + billing bits. :eyes:
ryan: happy to review. focus on QUIC fences and admission.
sheryl: I'll draft billing checkpoint rules.
sheryl: also note: we need a migration plan for older upstreams that ignore our headers — fallback to hard after soft_timeout.
matt: lgtm. also add tests for stream siblings not starving when one is canceled.
dana: thanks all — I'll open RFC this afternoon and link the canary checklist. :rocket:
